body.x: Daegu Metropolitan City will host the Future Innovation Tech Expo 2026 (FIX 2026) from October 21 to 24 at the EXCO convention center, marking its largest edition to date. Celebrating its third year, the four-day industrial exhibition convenes 588 participating enterprises across four core sectors: mobility, robotics, information and communication technology (ICT), and startups. Under the official theme “AI, Beyond Technology, Into Everyday Life,” the 2026 event highlights real-world industrial implementations and consumer applications of artificial intelligence, reflecting an expanding international presence, with overseas exhibitors representing 28% of total participants, up from 17% in the previous year.

The mobility segment, represented by the Daegu International Future Auto & Mobility Expo (DIFA), brings together major domestic manufacturers and tier-one suppliers alongside global automotive leaders. Hyundai Motor Company, GMTCK, SL Corporation, Sambo Motors, PHC, Kyung Chang Industrial, and L&F are exhibiting alongside Mercedes-Benz, Zeekr, Neolix, Volocopter, and DAS. Hyundai Motor Company is introducing developments in autonomous driving and vehicle software architectures, including its ATRIA AI and Pleos systems. Regional autonomous logistics partners RideFlux and Mars Auto are presenting autonomous freight trailers, while Neolix is unveiling its N3 and N6 autonomous robovans. Complementing these commercial showcases, the UAM Immersive Zone offers direct public flight simulations and boarding experiences featuring Volocopter’s Volocity electric air taxi airframe, as well as test-drive programs for electric vehicles from Mercedes-Benz and BYD.

In the robotics sector, designated as ROBEX, South Korea’s anchor industrial automation developers, HD Hyundai Robotics and Doosan Robotics, anchor the pavilion alongside physical AI innovators. HD Hyundai Robotics is demonstrating automated factory workflows using its next-generation HDC35-18 collaborative robot in a live tire-handling demonstration. Doosan Robotics is presenting five discrete automation systems, including its CES Best of Innovation Award-winning Scan&Go platform. Domestic humanoid developer A-Robot and specialized automation integrators HRT Robotics and Dogu Robotics are also exhibiting. At the same time, the Korea Institute for Robot Industry Advancement (KIRIA) features humanoid demonstration units executing tasks ranging from object sorting to gesture recognition.

The ICT exhibition, ITCE, features Asia’s largest cloud management service provider, Megazone Cloud, which is exhibiting its Megazone AIR integrated management platform alongside OnePredict’s commercialized industrial predictive AI solutions. The pavilion also features international delegations comprising 19 AI enterprises from Zhejiang, China, and 30 software firms representing ASEAN. Specialized regional initiatives include the PnGO unmanned robotic retail platform by AIRC and community-driven AI models from Pohang Technopark. In addition, telecommunications provider KT is operating the KT AI Station, a mobile education center focused on responsible AI deployment, deepfake detection, and media literacy.

Integrating early-stage venture ecosystems, the startup section brings together 91 global partners from 12 countries—including Thales, Alibaba Cloud, and Fund WA—to facilitate technical exchange and venture investment. The accompanying Startup Arena features 30 high-growth enterprises, including CES and FIX Innovation Award honorees Mobinn, Aims, Ziorobot, and Fix Robot. Running concurrently from October 21 to 23, the FIX 2026 International Conference features 60 speakers representing 17 countries, with keynote addresses by Professor Kyu-Jin Cho of Seoul National University, GMTCK President Brian McMurray, Vector Institute AI scholar Professor Xiaoxiao Li, PAL Robotics CEO Francesco Ferro, and Plug and Play Asia-Pacific Managing Partner Jupe Tan Sze Wei.

To drive commercial outcomes, the event has expanded its international export consultation meetings to a two-day schedule on October 22 and 23, matching exhibitors with 88 pre-qualified overseas buying organizations from 19 countries arranged through KOTRA and private trade agencies. In parallel, the Large Enterprise Procurement Consultation Session, supported by the Korea Commission for Corporate Partnership, convenes procurement directors from 50 domestic conglomerates—including Samsung SDI, POSCO, Lotte E&C, Hanwha, and SK Hynix—to evaluate SME technologies for integration into enterprise supply chains. Daegu Metropolitan City Mayor Kyung-ho Choo stated that FIX 2026 provides a platform to validate how artificial intelligence and advanced engineering are actively transforming production environments and daily living, affirming that the municipal government will continue leveraging the exhibition’s international business matching, technology transfer, and institutional procurement programs to position Daegu as a global capital for future innovation industries.
